start_here: Say to your AI: "Does my computer at 203.0.113.20 need a reboot after its updates? If it does and nothing is busy, reboot it and tell me it came back." It runs tool:reboot-a-computer-when-it-asks, first with mode read, then with mode reboot, and tells you what asked, whether it rebooted and anything that did not come back.
no_lists_because: It keeps nothing: it reads one computer, reboots it when it asks, and answers what it read before and after. The workflow that runs it at a quiet hour tells the people who share the computer first.
instructions: 1. Read the computer's row from wherever you keep it: its name, address and SSH host key.

2. Call tools:run with tool tool:reboot-a-computer-when-it-asks and input {name, address, host_key} (mode read is the default). The administrator key is the held value server-administration-ssh-key; it reaches only the hosts its vault entry names.
3. Read before.asks and before.packages: whether the computer's updates ask for a reboot. before.busy says what would make a reboot unsafe now.

4. To reboot, first tell whoever shares the computer and make sure no apply holds its row. Then call it again with mode reboot. It refuses a computer that does not ask (unless even_if_not_asked is true) or is busy, and says why.

5. Read rebooted, back_after_seconds and findings: still-asks-for-a-reboot, degraded-after-reboot, container-not-back, not-back-after-reboot. Then run tool:check-a-computer-from-inside to see each engine holds its person again.
